Prepare a study's AI table requests in one call

Source: R/ai_prepare.R
tfl_ai_prepare.Rd

The steps before the first request, one after the other: tfl_ai_study_init() (only when the study has no study.yml yet – one that is there is kept, so the call can be run again), tfl_ai_adam_summary() (to ai/adam_summary.md), tfl_ai_read_shell() (to ai/toc_shell.md; what it could not find is the result's hint), spec/toc.yml (the TOC's reports in order, with their section and analysis set, as tflplanner reads it; when the study has none) and tfl_ai_write_requests(). Nothing is sent anywhere.

Usage

tfl_ai_prepare(
  dir,
  toc,
  adam = "adam",
  study_id = "STUDY-01",
  title = NULL,
  toc_sheet = NULL,
  sheets = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  language = NULL,
  workbook = c("text", "file"),
  max_chars = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  dry_run = FALSE,
  adam_summary = NULL,
  datasets = NULL,
  max_levels = 15L,
  quiet = FALSE,
  shells = NULL,
  add = FALSE,
  templates = TRUE,
  progress = NULL,
  toc_cols = NULL,
  sheet_roles = NULL,
  unit = c("sheet", "toc"),
  area = TRUE,
  numbers = NULL,
  agent_reads = character(),
  docs = NULL,
  agent_max_reads = 3L,
  define = NULL,
  adam_spec = NULL
)

Arguments

dir

The study folder.

toc

The TOC / SHELL workbook (.xlsx or .xlsm).

adam

The ADaM folder, from dir (relative) or absolute.

study_id, title

The study's id and title, for a new study folder.

toc_sheet, sheets

As tfl_ai_read_shell(): the TOC sheet when the guess is wrong, the sheets to keep.

size, language, workbook, max_chars

As tfl_ai_write_requests(): the reports a request holds (NULL, the default: 1), the language of the assumptions – and of the agent's questions in the chat: it is written to study.yml as ai: language –, how the workbook reaches the agent ("text", "file"; with "workbook" in agent_reads, "text" is "file": the text and each shell's place in the workbook file), a request's length at most.

overwrite

TRUE to start the study folder again (tfl_ai_study_init() over its study.yml and spec/). The requests are written again on every call (the drafts are kept).

dry_run

TRUE to read the workbook and the ADaM and write nothing: the same result, to look at before the requests are written (its requests are the TOC's batches, without chars and file; files is empty).

adam_summary

A tfl_ai_adam_summary() result to use instead of reading the ADaM again (a previous call's $adam); read again when datasets names others than it has.

datasets, max_levels

As tfl_ai_adam_summary(): the ADaM datasets the requests describe (NULL: all), the values listed of a variable. Fewer datasets, shorter requests.

quiet

TRUE to say nothing (the steps' messages): a screen shows the result's hint and next_steps itself.

shells

Workbooks holding the shells when toc holds the TOC alone (as tfl_ai_read_shell()): each report's shell is looked for in them; the requests and the toc say each report's book.

add

TRUE to add this workbook's reports to the study's requests and drafts already there (a TOC of listings, a book of PK figures, one at a time): the new requests are named after those there (ae-2), a report asked for already stops the call (overwrite = TRUE asks for it again), spec/toc.yml gets the new reports at its end, and the workbook's text is ai/toc_shell-<workbook>.md. With add, overwrite is about the requests alone: the study's study.yml, spec/data.yml, spec/defaults.yml and the agent's files are kept as they are.

templates

TRUE (default): the agent writes a report with one of the study's templates where it fits (template: {name, args}, and the report's own content items for what it does not cover), else as a code SPEC; the requests (and AGENTS.md) list the templates registered now – tflspec's, a company's, the study's variants. FALSE: the code SPEC only, the requests as they were before templates. The setting is each request's first line (templates: TRUE) and ai/status.md's.

progress

NULL, or a function(step, i, n) called as the work goes: step "adam" (the ADaM's summary), "workbook" (the TOC / SHELL read), then "request", i of n requests written – for a progress bar (shiny's setProgress()); see tfl_ai_write_requests().

toc_cols

The TOC's columns, when its headers do not say them (as tfl_ai_read_shell()): c(output_id = "Output No", shell = "Shell", title = c("Title 1", "Title 2")), a header's text or a column's letter.

sheet_roles

As tfl_ai_read_shell(): sheets' roles over the guess.

unit

A request's unit: "sheet" (default) a shell sheet – what the sheet writes first, then its name, then its TOC candidates (the TOC and the sheet names can hold mistakes), the reports and their ids the AI's to read from it – and one request of the TOC items no sheet chose; "toc" the TOC's reports, as before (a report's shell found by its number).

area

Where the agent's drafts go: TRUE (the default), their own folder ai/spec/outputs/ (made here), built into ai/output/, which the person adopts into the study's spec/outputs/ (tfl_ai_adopt()); FALSE, the folder is not made here (a study of the form before is moved with tfl_ai_migrate()).

numbers

The person's check of the report numbers each shell sheet writes (see the result's numbers), over the rule (a number written in the sheet or its name, and a TOC item's, is a report of the sheet's request): a data frame with sheet, number and make – FALSE, the number is a reference only (the request still shows it, not as one of its reports); TRUE, a report of that sheet's request (a TOC item the rule left a candidate, or a number no TOC item has, which is warned of and keeps its number as the sheet writes it as its id); NA, back to the rule – or a list named by sheet, each the numbers that sheet makes (its other numbers references only). The numbers and sheets not given keep the rule. The result's toc follows: a TOC item made in a sheet has that sheet as its shell (made in several, the first in the workbook's order; the others listed in sheets), one the rule made and no sheet makes now has none (the no-shell request's, counted in counts). Saved as ai/sheet_numbers.csv (sheet, number, make, UTF-8) when the requests are written (not by a dry run), and read by a later call; given again, it goes over the saved rows (a row of the same sheet and number replaced, NA taking it out) and the file keeps the result. NULL (default): the saved file, if any. With unit = "sheet" only.

agent_reads

What the agent may open besides the requests and the files they name: "workbook" (the TOC / SHELL workbook: each request then says where its shells are in it) and "adam" (the ADaM), read only to settle what a request leaves unclear, with whatever tool the PC has (PowerShell, Python, R). character() (default): neither, and AGENTS.md says not to open them.

docs

Documents the agent may read for what a request leaves unclear (a SAP, a data guide): their paths. A study's documents live in the study folder (its docs/): one inside the folder is read where it is, never copied – a .md / .txt at its own path; a .docx, .pdf or workbook, which an agent in the editor cannot read, as its text written to ai/docs/<name>.md (tfl_ai_doc_text(): the headings and tables kept). One outside the study folder is copied into ai/docs/ (the agent works in the study folder), the text beside it for those kinds. AGENTS.md names what the agent reads and which document a text stands for; the agent reads no other document. NULL (default): none.

agent_max_reads

How many times for a request the agent may open a file or run a command beyond the request and the files it names; then it asks, or marks what is unclear to confirm, and goes on. Default 3.

define, adam_spec

The study's define.xml, or its ADaM spec workbook (Pinnacle 21 layout), for the ADaM summary (tfl_ai_adam_summary()): its code lists in their order with their decodes, and the digits and display formats, value level too (a parameter's AVAL), go into ai/adam_summary.md as the study's. NULL (default): the data alone.

Value

A tfl_ai_prepared: a list with requests (one row a request: request, family, outputs – the TOC items it names (a sheet's: its candidates) –, n, chars, file, sheets – as tfl_ai_write_requests() gives them), toc (one row a TOC item: toc_id, title, type, toc_sheets, sheets – the shell sheets it is a candidate of –, shell, shell_found, request – the requests naming it, NA for none –, book, shell_id, population, program, file, info as tfl_ai_read_shell()'s toc says them), shells (a row a shell sheet, as tfl_ai_read_shell()'s, with its request), numbers (a row a report number a shell sheet writes or its name has: sheet, number as the sheet writes it, title – the TOC item's, else the sheet's own when it writes that number alone, else NA –, toc_id – the TOC item it is, NA none –, make – a report of that sheet's request –, source – "rule", "guess" (a TOC item no sheet writes or names, whose number – a part letter taken off, 15.2.4.2.b – sheets write, each number (a part with its letter) on its own: made the best sheet's, its id the number the sheet writes, the other sheets' a candidate each, not made; the best: an exact number before one a part letter differs, in the sheet's title rows or name before its body only, then the sheet whose own number is nearest, then the first in the workbook), "saved" (ai/sheet_numbers.csv) or "given" (numbers) –, reason – a guess's: how it matches, "not an exact match" when not, its choice among the sheets; "set by the person" for "saved" and "given"; NA the rule's –; a dry run's and the written requests' alike), counts (shells, toc_items, no_shell), sheets (the workbook's sheets and their roles), adam (the tfl_ai_adam_summary(): datasets, variables, text), files (the files written, relative to dir), hint (what the workbook's reading could not find – no TOC, a report with no shell – and what to pass), next_steps (what to do next), agent_prompt (the first message to the agent, its paths from the study folder (a copy of the study says the same), also written to ai/agent_prompt.md) and agent_files (what the agent may open besides the requests and the files they name, from the study folder: the workbook and the ADaM as agent_reads allows, and the documents; character() else). Its print is the workbook's summary and the next step. The files are UTF-8.

The agent's work

The requests are for a coding agent (GitHub Copilot's agent in VS Code, and the like) that asks the person in the chat what defines each report and is not settled – the analysis set, a parameter, the treatment variable, a denominator – waits for the answers, keeps them in ai/decisions.md (tfl_ai_decisions_read()) and applies them to the reports after, then writes each report's skeleton as a draft, ai/spec/outputs/<id>.yml: its data, its analyses, the items that make its rows (or a template), its titles and footnotes – nothing of the look. What it could not settle it marks under the draft's ai: confirm (tfl_ai_confirm()). The person checks the drafts (tflplanner's "Check", tfl_ai_collect_answers()), finishes them in the builder and adopts them (tfl_ai_adopt()).

Besides the requests (each starting with the agent's steps and the decisions that apply to its reports), and what every request would repeat written once for the agent to read – ai/instructions-table.md and ai/instructions-figure.md (the instructions, the schema, what a draft holds), ai/templates.md (with templates = TRUE: every template, each request naming the ones likely for its reports), ai/adam_summary.md and spec/, each request naming them – the study folder gets ai/AGENTS.md (the instructions: what the agent reads, how it asks, what a draft holds), AGENTS.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md (short: read ai/AGENTS.md), run.R (tfl_ai_run(): the check from the command line, with the ARD and RTF) and ai/decisions.md, which is never written over. One message (ai/agent_prompt.md) starts the agent on every request of ai/requests/index.md in order; stopped, it goes on at "continue" from the first request with a draft missing.

study.yml's ai: keys set the agent's rules (the study standard's spec/defaults.yml may say them under its own ai: key first): language (the chat's: "en", "ja" ...), ask_when ("request", the default: the request's reports' questions together; "report": report by report), carry (which decision scopes apply to a later report without asking: all, dataset, section), max_rounds (how many times one item is asked again, 3), footnotes_at ("footer", the default, or "table": where the shell's footnotes go).

See also

The AI table guide: system.file("ai", "tflspec-ai-table-guide.md", package = "tflspec").

Examples

# \donttest{
# (over 5 seconds: the workbook read, five ADaM written, every request)
ex <- system.file("ai", "example", package = "tflspec")
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "prepare-study")
dir.create(file.path(d, "adam"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (requireNamespace("haven", quietly = TRUE)) {
  for (x in c("adsl", "adae", "adrs", "adlb", "adtte")) {
    df <- getExportedValue("tflspec", x)
    for (v in names(df)) if (is.factor(df[[v]])) df[[v]] <- as.character(df[[v]])
    haven::write_xpt(df, file.path(d, "adam", paste0(x, ".xpt")))
  }
  r <- tfl_ai_prepare(d, file.path(ex, "onco_toc_shell.xlsx"),
                      study_id = "XYZ-ONC-01", overwrite = TRUE)
  r$requests[c("request", "outputs", "chars")]
}
#> 4 requests (5 reports) in ai/requests; the longest 4885 characters.
#> Next: give the agent ai/requests/T14.1.1.md (ai/agent_prompt.md); when its drafts are written, run tfl_ai_collect_answers().
#>   request            outputs chars
#> 1 T14.1.1           T-14-1-1  4676
#> 2 T14.2.1           T-14-2-1  4549
#> 3  Safety T-14-3-1, T-14-3-5  5412
#> 4 F14.2.2           F-14-2-2  3927
# }
